title: Introduce invocation snapshot reservoir and rate-aware alert calibrator
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a reservoir sampling-based invocation snapshot store for targeted debugging and a rate-aware alert calibrator to reduce alert noise during traffic surges. New dashboard tiles and migration steps included.
notes: Staged rollout behind feature flag; 20% telemetry traffic initially. No schema migrations. Remove flag after 2 weeks of stable telemetry.
body:
Motivation: We see chronic alert noise and blind spots for large but infrequent invocation spikes. Engineers need representative snapshots from long-tailed invocations without blowing up storage or cardinality. This PR introduces a lightweight in-memory+redis-backed invocation snapshot reservoir sampler and a downstream rate-aware alert calibrator that dampens alert churn during expected surges.

What this changes (high level): Adds a reservoir sampler that keeps prioritized invocation snapshots (compact metadata + compressed log excerpt) per endpoint cohort. Adds an alert calibrator service that adjusts alert thresholds and suppression windows based on observed invocation rate envelopes and reservoir fullness. Ships dashboards: reservoir occupancy, sampled invocation types, calibrator adjustments, and a new "Representative Snapshots" UI tile for quick repro links.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc (ENG-4821) reviewed 
- [x] Unit & integration tests 
- [x] Dashboard panels and grafana queries 
- [x] Feature flag gating and staged rollout plan 
- [x] Runbook updated for SRE playbooks

Design notes: Reservoir sampling: each cohort (service:route:model_variant) has an independent reservoir with a size cap (configurable). We use Vitter's Algorithm R for streaming sampling and attach a lightweight priority computed from token-cost-weight and anomaly-score. Snapshots are stored compressed in a TTL-backed store (redis stream + object blob store for large excerpts). The sampler emits metrics: reservoir_size, reservoir_evictions, sample_rate, and snapshot_payload_bytes.

Calibrator: The calibrator consumes per-cohort rate histograms and reservoir occupancy. It outputs adjustment signals: threshold_delta_pct and quiet_window_ms which are applied by the existing alerting pipeline via an adapter. The calibrator supports two modes: passive (recommend-only) and active (applies adjustments via API). Default is passive; the rollout uses passive mode for 1 week then switches to active for non-critical alerts.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy sampler + calibrator in passive mode behind feature flag (feature:invocation_snapshot_reservoir). 2) Enable dashboard tiles and synthetic replay to validate sample representativeness. 3) Gradually open reservoir write traffic: 10% -> 50% -> 100%. 4) Switch calibrator to active for low-severity alert groups. 5) Iterate on thresholds and reservoir sizing.

Testing: Unit tests for sampling correctness and priority handling included. Integration tests exercise the redis-backed store and calibrator's effect on simulated rate bursts. Replay bench runs used real invocation shapes (see ENG-4879).

Backward compatibility & migration: No changes to persisted event schemas consumed by downstream analytics. Snapshots are opaque objects; telemetry consumers that opt-in can dereference blobs via the new snapshot API. The feature is fully reversible by toggling the feature flag and draining reservoirs.

Commit summary: See commits list for granular messages.

Files changed (summary): Added sampler core, calibrator service, API adapter, feature flagging, dashboard panels, unit/integration tests, and runbook updates.

Why this is different from previous work: Instead of capturing every detailed trace, we keep bounded representative snapshots prioritized by cost and anomaly score, and we explicitly couple that with rate-aware alert adjustments. This reduces storage/cardinality concerns while giving engineers actionable examples for debugging long-tail incidents.

Operational notes: Reservoir metrics are exported to the existing telemetry namespace under telemetry.reservoir.*. Calibrator emits decision traces as sampling spans so SRE can trace why an adjustment fired. We added a safeguard: alerts that directly touch billing/chargeback remain exempt from active dampening.

Merge notes: Squash-merged. Post-merge: enable feature flag to 10% and monitor reservoir_evictions and alert_firings for 72 hours.

Maya Patel (2026-02-18): Responded - switched to context propagation and added a memory benchmark in reservoir_test.go. See commit b2c3d4e.
Jordan Liu (2026-02-20): Approve after CI stable. Asked to ensure calibrator logs the decision reason and exposes it in traces.
Priya Nandakumar (2026-02-24): Suggested making the default reservoir size smaller (100 -> 50) and making per-tenant cap configurable. Updated configs accordingly.
SRE Bot (2026-02-25): Integration tests passed on staging; noted high eviction rate for one tenant during replay. Reduced that tenant's sample rate during staged rollout.
